sources.citation: Sellato, Bernard & Antonia Soriente. 2015. The languages and peoples of the Müller Mountains; A contribution to the study of the origins of Borneo's nomads and their languages. Wacana 16(2): 339-354. doi:10.17510/wacana.v16i2.381
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Punan Merah is only named (p.347) as a member of the Bukat-Beketan-Lisum (BBL) cluster: 'Related to Bukat... are the languages of the Beketan..., Lisum of the Tabang area, Punan Merah, Punan Kohi, and several more.' No Punan Merah data; Table 6 (p.348) gives segmental features for Lisum, not Punan Merah. The paper's only stress statement (p.344) is about Seputan (MSP cluster): 'its strong stress on the penultimate syllable.' Nothing on Punan Merah or Lisum stress.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: A Comprehensive Classification. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Mānoa.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Punan Merah appears once (p.37) inside the Ethnologue-derived 'Müller-Schwaner Punan' listing (Aoheng, Bukat, Hovongan, Kereho, Punan Aput, Punan Merah). Smith's Punan chapter (sec. 2.4) is built on his own Punan Lisum wordlist (Long Sule, Belayan tributary of the Mahakam, consultant Ilip Asung, p.15) plus Punan Aput, Beketan, Ukit, Buket, Punan Bah, Punan Tubu; historical vowel phonology only. No stress statement for any Punan dialect (the dissertation's stress remarks concern Merap, Segai-Modang, Hliboi Bidayuh and West-Kalimantan Malayic).

sources.citation: Rensch, Calvin R. 2012. Melanau and the Languages of Central Sarawak. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012-011. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: Does not mention Punan Merah at all; only 'Lisum appears to be similar to Bukat' (lexicostatistic remark). No stress.

sources.citation: Chan, Henry. 2007. Survival in the Rainforest: Change and Resilience among the Punan Vuhang of Eastern Sarawak, Malaysia. PhD diss., University of Helsinki.
sources.note: Lisum mentioned only as a historical nomadic group killed/absorbed by Iban; no Punan Merah, no language data.
Four references, none descriptive: Sellato & Sercombe 2007 and Rensch 2012 (subclassification comments), Campbell et al. 2022 and Lewis 2009 (endangerment). Nothing on stress.
